newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece ready for possible Albanian refugee influx.
newsitem.headline: Greece ready for possible Albanian refugee influx.

text.p: Greece said on Friday it was ready to receive Albanians fleeing violence in their Balkan country although there was no sign of a mass exodus.
"We don't foresee a wave of refugees coming," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas told reporters. "But we are prepared to cope with it if it does."
Reppas said Greece had responded positively to a request from the Geneva-based U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) and was already taking measures and preparing camps.
Greece, already taxed with about 350,000 Albanians, mostly illegal workers, is gravely concerned over the crisis across its northern border.
But there has been no great wave of refugees from Albania since violence swept the south, prompted by the collapse of fraudulent pyramid investment schemes.
The U.N. refugee agency said on Friday it had urged Albania's neighbours Greece and Italy to allow Albanians fleeing violence and anarchy to enter and stay "as long as necessary".
The UNHCR said Italy had identified a shelter site near a former military airport at Bari-Palese, which can hold up to 1,000 people, while Greece was planning facilities for 3,000 in the north.
